A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ATPrompt despite the changed title and terminology. All 15 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ATPrompt classification experiments, cross-dataset and domain-generalization results, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original ATPrompt experiments and reports additional baseline integrations and revised attribute-choice ablation results.

M1.justification: The attribute-class prompt construction, shallow/deep token handling, cross-entropy objective, and alternating differentiable attribute search remain unchanged. The additional baseline integrations reuse this construction; no new ATPrompt-specific algorithmic component is described. Renaming embedded attributes as anchored attributes does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 recognition datasets plus ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-A, and ImageNet-R, with the same three generalization tasks. Domain generalization moves from v1's appendix to v2's main text. The expanded attribute ablation reuses already covered datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons with ArGue, DePT, CoPrompt, and PromptKD. DePT and PromptKD replace KgCoOp and PromptSRC as ATPrompt integration baselines. KgCoOp disappears from the table, while PromptSRC remains only without ATPrompt. The cross-dataset and domain-generalization comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 changes the reported search budget from 40 to 10 epochs, although Table 13 changes its caption from 40 to 20 epochs, leaving the actual schedule unresolved. The attribute-choice comparison changes from Food101 results to averages across 11 datasets, and DePT introduces additional training configurations. Principal splits and metrics remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The common-versus-irrelevant-versus-searched attribute ablation expands from Food101 in v1 Table 7 to 11-dataset averages in v2 Table 8, while dropping the leather/silk condition. Other ablations retain their evidence. V2's expanded appendix attribute-order table merely combines results already present in v1's main text and appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy and harmonic means averaged over three runs. Neither introduces seed identities, confidence intervals, reported variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds and removes substantial result sets, including new DePT+ATPrompt and PromptKD+ATPrompt average HMs of 78.45 and 84.35. MaPLe+ATPrompt's reported average HM changes from 79.10 to 79.21. The attribute ablation supplies new 11-dataset averages, which are not directly comparable to v1's Food101 scores. Cross-dataset and domain-generalization numbers remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, prompt construction, search relaxation, and alternating updates retain their substance. V2 replaces explicit front/middle prompt equations with prose describing the retained configurations and adds a combination-count formula explaining the existing search space. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that universal attributes improve unseen-category alignment through a compatible, inexpensive prompt-format plug-in, supported by differentiable attribute selection and shallow/deep variants. The renamed terminology and revised supporting comparisons do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for ImageNet attributes transferring across datasets and explicitly acknowledges weaker standalone performance than regularization-based methods and manually chosen anchor positions. It revises the explanation for limited gains toward the role of additional baseline modules. Earlier future directions involving multimodal LLMs and implicit attributes remain.

D1.justification: The hardware description changes from V100 to A800, and search timing changes from about 40 minutes to often under five minutes under different reported conditions. V2 adds DePT hyperparameters, removes KgCoOp/PromptSRC implementation sections, and omits the explicit default-backbone statement. Its new PromptKD integration lacks corresponding implementation details. The project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds TAP and additional architecture-search and distillation references, and expands the discussion of ArGue, including its learning targets and ensembling. These additions sharpen the distinction between universal attributes as prompt components and class-specific attribute supervision; the underlying research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites existing search, implementation, discussion, and conclusion passages, changes the title and terminology throughout, and edits authorship and affiliation text. It reorganizes the search explanation into named components, moves domain generalization into the main experimental narrative, and introduces a main-text limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned from paired method columns into three dataset blocks with method rows. Figure 2 adds an ArGue comparison panel, and appendix Figure 9 replaces the PromptSRC diagram with DePT. Domain-generalization results move into the main text, while multiple appendix displays are rearranged or consolidated.

improvement.justification: V2 provides better comparative context through ArGue and other additional baselines, extends the attribute-choice ablation beyond Food101, and more clearly states standalone-performance and anchor-placement limitations. These strengthen assessment of the retained method. The gain is limited by unreconciled 10-versus-20-epoch search reporting and missing implementation details for the new PromptKD integration, which weaken reproducibility.
